summary: Donald K. Swearer worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying under mentors Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Singkha Wannasai. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004), Chiang Mai University, and Harvard University (2004–2010).

Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University (~1938–1951) under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard University (~1946–1947). He held appointments at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (1955).

A philosopher, Donald Phillip Verene earned his bachelor's from Knox College (~1955–1959) and his doctorate from Washington University in St. Louis (~1959–1964). He served as chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting posts at Pembroke College and the University of Rome.

Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Patrick Olivelle, Ludo Rocher, and Richard W. Lariviere, and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006–2012).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Donald S. Lopez, Jr. completed his degrees under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia. He held faculty posts at Middlebury College (1986), the University of Bristol (1997), and the University of Michigan (1990).
Donald Wiebe is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He served on the faculty at Trinity College, Toronto (~1980–2018) and was general editor of Toronto Studies in Religion (~1986).
Dondub Buddhayin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as abbot at Chilttai Monastery and at Ganden Dargye Ling (attested 1933).

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Tendzin studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and also taught the latter two scholars.

Dongchu was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Institute (~1936–1945) and abbot of Dinghui Temple (~1945–1949).

Dongmei Fang was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under John Dewey at the University of Nanking and earned an MA from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He held posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

Donna C. Kurtz is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Cincinnati, Yale University, and Somerville College, Oxford. She held a post at the Classical Art Research Centre (~1979–2011).

Dor Bahadur Bista worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies after studying at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He was a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1978–1990) and served on the board of governors of ICIMOD (~1983–1989).
Doranne Jacobson works in Indology and anthropology. She earned her doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan studied at Hunter College and the University of Pennsylvania. Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, she held posts at Columbia, Barnard, George Washington University, George Mason University, Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, and Stony Brook University (~2007).
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.
Dorje Rinchen was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under teachers including Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Ja Shong Lob Zur Lodrö Gyatso, and Chime Tenpai Nyima.

Dorje Tseten was a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied education at Beijing Normal University (~1944–1948) and served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He attended First Kazan Male Gymnasium and Kazan Imperial University (~1842–1846), completing his doctoral dissertation under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski.
